input_and_result_semantics: The existing knowledge-injection route and CLI gain opt-in exact inputs. Existing native prompt algorithms, legacy defaults and explicit provider controls remain available.

A confirmed pre-existing HTTP multipart bug discarded partial opening boundaries. The scoped parser fix retains a bounded suffix until the complete marker arrives; one-byte chunks, every initial split and preambles have native regression coverage. Filename-presence metadata separately retains empty versus absent filenames.
Assumptions preserve vector order, duplicates and empty elements. Context accepts NativeString key/value pairs, rejects duplicate decoded keys and follows native map byte ordering.

Independent assumptions/context JSON or actual File controls combine with the existing six scalar controls. Full options require exactly all eight native fields and conflict by presence with individual controls.

Native strings preserve empty, whitespace, Unicode, NUL, arbitrary bytes and WTF8 through literal or hex-v1 carriers. Original input bytes and File metadata remain separate from canonical native options.

Byte bounds retain exact native unsigned decimal values, including values beyond JavaScript safe integers. Positive bounds are inclusive; zero retains the native exception. Inactive scalar values still count toward input bytes.

The exact envelope retains complete successful and computed=false native results, input/prompt byte counts, configured options and original controls. Parser and native exceptions remain failures with retained available provenance.

Actual File channels require multipart filename presence, including an explicit empty filename. Scalar and JSON multipart byte fields may carry filenames; transport filename provenance remains separate from the File role.

The existing HTTP library normalizes byte-identical raw query pairs before parameter handling. Distinct observable occurrences, duplicate decoded keys, mutually exclusive channels and full/individual control conflicts are rejected.

Both public helpers preserve original File objects, source hashes, exact response text and complete reports. Native prompt and original serializer bytes have direct downloads independent of presentation/transport errors.

The shared PromptChat extends both traditional and OCEL paths and retains ContextBuilder provenance. The native knowledge kernel has no OCEL File argument; no invented native log consumption is claimed.

Authoritative native output is separate from editable provider text. Only an explicit copy action creates a Unicode provider version with normalized editor line endings. Invalid UTF8/WTF8 stays inspectable/downloadable without replacement-decoded automatic sending.

Feature validation makes no external provider calls. Direct native witnesses and API, CLI and client captures do not establish complete external reference behavior, browser, performance or concurrency parity.
